| Task | `ours` time (geometric mean) | Strongest competitor | Its time (geometric mean) | Speed against it (its time ÷ ours; higher is better) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| generic load | 100 ns | `rival 2.0` | 100 ns | 1.00× (level) | ◆ mixed (partial: a workload has no number) |
| dump | 90 ns | `other 3.0` | 100 ns | 1.11× faster | ▲ win |
| patch (RFC 6902) | — | — | — | — | NOT COMPARABLE |

Not in a row's mean: generic load: no number: `w4` (differs); patch (RFC 6902): no number: `w1` (unsupported).

Each row is the geometric mean, over the real-world workloads the task has, of our time and of the time of the strongest competitor in each workload. Speed is the competitor's time divided by ours: 2× faster means half the time, and a loss is stated as slower. Where several competitors were strongest the column names them all, with how often. A † marks a cell measured differently from the task as specified; the note beside each mark says how. A marked competitor still counts. A workload where our library has no number is listed and the row is marked as partial, never counted as a win. The verdict is never better than the per-workload verdicts allow: a row with a losing workload is marked mixed or loss, and a row with no winning workload is never marked a win. The speed is over the real-world workloads. The verdict is never better than the real-world workloads allow, nor better than all of the task's workloads allow, generated and reference ones included: a loss on any of them keeps a row from being a clean win and the row says how many it lost, and a win on them cannot lift a row the real-world workloads do not win. Memory and the count of better, level and worse workloads in each row are on the full page.

Method: **full run** of 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z. Kit 0.9.0 (revision abc); text generated by kit revision 0123456789ab. `ours 1.0`; competitors `rival 2.0`, `other 3.0`. Runtime rustc x (target t), measured with criterion: tm. Memory: mm. Test CPU (4 logical CPUs, 8.0 GiB), Linux (x86_64), host load (1 min) 0.5 before, 0.5 after.

<desc>ours: speed per task against the strongest competitor. Times faster than the strongest competitor on each task (geometric mean over its real-world workloads), log scale: bars to the right are faster, higher is better, bars to the left are slower. The mark beside a bar counts every workload of the task, generated and reference ones included. Unchanged emit times the write path of a document that was not edited; a library that keeps the text returns it without rendering, so it is not a rendering speed. A † marks a cell measured differently from the task as specified. generic load 1.00× (level) mixed (ours 100 ns vs 100 ns; workloads: 2 better, 0 level, 1 worse of 3; the speed is over the 2 real-world workloads and the mark counts all 3; partial, no number for w4 (differs)); dump 1.11× faster win (ours 90 ns vs 100 ns; workloads: 1 better, 0 level, 0 worse of 1); patch (RFC 6902) NOT COMPARABLE (w1 unsupported).
